verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.44
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 10.44

verses.pali: 5. Akkosavagga
verses.english: 5. Abuse

verses.pali: Kusinārasutta
verses.english: At Kusinārā

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kusinārāyaṁ viharati baliharaṇe vanasaṇḍe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kusinārā, in the Forest of Offerings.

verses.pali: Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

verses.pali: “bhikkhavo”ti.
verses.english: “Mendicants!”

verses.pali: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Venerable sir,” they replied.

verses.pali: Bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Codakena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ paccavekkhitvā pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo.
verses.english: “Mendicants, a mendicant who wants to accuse another should first check five things in themselves and establish five things in themselves.

verses.pali: Katame pañca dhammā ajjhattaṁ paccavekkhitabbā?
verses.english: What five things should they check in themselves?

verses.pali: Codakena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena evaṁ paccavekkhitabbaṁ:
verses.english: A mendicant who wants to accuse another should check this:

verses.pali: ‘parisuddhakāyasamācāro nu khomhi, parisuddhenamhi kāyasamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṁsena.
verses.english: ‘Is my bodily behavior pure? Do I have pure bodily behavior that is impeccable and irreproachable?

verses.pali: Saṁvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti?
verses.english: Is this thing found in me or not?’

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti parisuddhena kāyasamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṁsena, tassa bhavanti vattāro:
verses.english: If it’s not, there will be people who say:

verses.pali: ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā kāyikaṁ sikkhassū’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro.
verses.english: ‘Come on, venerable, train your own bodily behavior first.’

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, codakena bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena evaṁ paccavekkhitabbaṁ:
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant who wants to accuse another should check this:

verses.pali: ‘parisuddhavacīsamācāro nu khomhi, parisuddhenamhi vacīsamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṁsena.
verses.english: ‘Is my verbal behavior pure? Do I have pure verbal behavior that is impeccable and irreproachable?

verses.pali: Saṁvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti?
verses.english: Is this thing found in me or not?’

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parisuddhavacīsamācāro hoti parisuddhena vacīsamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṁsena, tassa bhavanti vattāro:
verses.english: If it’s not, there will be people who say:

verses.pali: ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā vācasikaṁ sikkhassū’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro.
verses.english: ‘Come on, venerable, train your own verbal behavior first.’

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, codakena bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena evaṁ paccavekkhitabbaṁ:
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant who wants to accuse another should check this:

verses.pali: ‘mettaṁ nu kho me cittaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ sabrahmacārīsu anāghātaṁ.
verses.english: ‘Is my heart established in love for my spiritual companions, without resentment?

verses.pali: Saṁvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti?
verses.english: Is this thing found in me or not?’

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṁ cittaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu anāghātaṁ, tassa bhavanti vattāro:
verses.english: If it’s not, there will be people who say:

verses.pali: ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā sabrahmacārīsu mettaṁ cittaṁ upaṭṭhāpehī’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro.
verses.english: ‘Come on, venerable, establish your heart in love for your spiritual companions first.’

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, codakena bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena evaṁ paccavekkhitabbaṁ:
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant who wants to accuse another should check this:

verses.pali: ‘bahussuto nu khomhi sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpā me dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
verses.english: ‘Am I very learned, remembering and keeping what I’ve learned? These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. Am I very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically?

verses.pali: Saṁvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti?
verses.english: Is this thing found in me or not?’

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, tassa bhavanti vattāro:
verses.english: If it’s not, there will be people who say:

verses.pali: ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā āgamaṁ pariyāpuṇassū’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro.
verses.english: ‘Come on, venerable, memorize the scriptures first.’

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, codakena bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena evaṁ paccavekkhitabbaṁ:
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant who wants to accuse another should check this:

verses.pali: ‘ubhayāni kho pana me pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso.
verses.english: ‘Have both monastic codes been passed down to me in detail, well analyzed, well mastered, and well evaluated in both the rules and accompanying material?

verses.pali: Saṁvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti?
verses.english: Is this thing found in me or not?’

verses.pali: No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ubhayāni pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, ‘idaṁ panāyasmā, kattha vuttaṁ bhagavatā’ti, iti puṭṭho na sampāyissati.
verses.english: If it’s not, and if they are unable to respond when asked “Venerable, where was this spoken by the Buddha?” there will be people who say:

verses.pali: Tassa bhavanti vattāro:
‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā vinayaṁ sikkhassū’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro.
verses.english: ‘Come on, venerable, train in the monastic code first.’

verses.pali: Ime pañca dhammā ajjhattaṁ paccavekkhitabbā.
verses.english: These are the five things they should check in themselves.

verses.pali: Katame pañca dhammā ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhāpetabbā?
verses.english: What five things should they establish in themselves?

verses.pali: ‘Kālena vakkhāmi, no akālena;
verses.english: ‘I will speak at the right time, not at the wrong time.

verses.pali: bhūtena vakkhāmi, no abhūtena;
verses.english: I will speak truthfully, not falsely.

verses.pali: saṇhena vakkhāmi, no pharusena;
verses.english: I will speak gently, not harshly.

verses.pali: atthasaṁhitena vakkhāmi, no anatthasaṁhitena;
verses.english: I will speak beneficially, not harmfully.

verses.pali: mettacitto vakkhāmi, no dosantaro’ti—
verses.english: I will speak lovingly, not from secret hate.’

verses.pali: ime pañca dhammā ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhāpetabbā.
verses.english: These are the five things they should establish in themselves.

verses.pali: Codakena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ paccavekkhitvā ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo”ti.
verses.english: A mendicant who wants to accuse another should first check these five things in themselves and establish these five things in themselves.”

verses.pali: Catutthaṁ.
